phase: Phase 2 — Transfer Attempts, Fencing, Integrity, and Reconciliation
checkpoint: authoritative attempts, atomic assignment, fenced agent protocol, and atomic multi-entity lifecycle reporting

tddCompliance.method: Each behavior was first expressed by a failing component or real HTTP-boundary test and its red output was retained. Production changes were then limited to making that behavior pass, followed by focused regression, external-path, clean affected-module, and JaCoCo verification.
tddCompliance.acceptanceStatement: A committed transfer attempt has immutable ordered evidence; assignment and its first attempt are created atomically; polling supplies attempt, lease, fence, and sequence context; reports require expected state, fence, and sequence; stale or expired agents are rejected; report acceptance is atomic across attempt, assignment, transfer status, and progress; exact terminal retries are safe through HTTP; and authorized callers can inspect attempt evidence through the real controller boundary.

subsequentGreen.outcome: passed after preserving the legacy invalid-transition conflict contract

refactor: Added the new sealed command subtype to the existing exhaustive serialization-dispatch assertion without introducing a default branch.
Recognized exact report retries before active-fence validation while still requiring the persisted fencing generation and exact authoritative result fields.
Replaced the generic terminal-outcome predicate with an exhaustive state-to-outcome mapping.
Exposed the immutable read model through two tenant-checked nested HTTP resources and synchronized OpenAPI plus endpoint discovery; both inherit the established transfers:read authorization scope.
Added focused core model characterization after the behavioral slice was green so the module-local JaCoCo report measures the immutable model directly.
Extended the assignment command rather than creating a second write so the assignment and first attempt share one deterministic Raft entry.
Carried one attempt context object through polling and reporting so the agent increments report sequences in one place.
Translated authoritative stale-fence, sequence, lease, and state rejections into stable HTTP conflicts.
Stabilized the leader-guard test fixture by separating the intended leader election timeout from follower timeouts; the isolated seven-test suite then passed.
Replaced the attempt-aware sequence of independent writes with one lifecycle report command that validates every referenced entity and transition before mutating any state.
Allowed a terminal retry to resolve its inactive historical attempt by request identity and delegated exact-retry recognition to the authoritative state application.
